headline: This law makes 988 the national number for suicide prevention and mental health crisis calls.
what_it_does: The law requires the Federal Communications Commission to designate 988 as the universal phone number for a national suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline. States may charge and collect a fee for 988 services, but the money must go into a separate account and be spent only on 988 services. The law also requires reports on how to run 988 well nationwide and on a plan to reach high-risk groups such as LGBTQ youth, minority communities, and rural residents.

who_it_affects.group: People in crisis or thinking about suicide
who_it_affects.how: They can call or text 988 as a single, easy-to-remember number to reach a crisis hotline.

who_it_affects.group: Families and friends of people in crisis
who_it_affects.how: They have one national number to call when they are worried about someone's mental health.
States may impose and collect fees for 988 services, but must hold that money in a designated account and use it only for 988 services.
The FCC must designate 988 as the universal number and submit an annual report on how states administer 988 fees.
The Department of Veterans Affairs must work with HHS on a joint report about making 988 operate effectively across the country.

who_it_affects.group: LGBTQ youth, minority communities, and rural residents
who_it_affects.how: HHS must develop a strategy to give these high-risk groups access to competent, specialized crisis services.
